title: Scope, Scope Chain & Hoisting
html:
Scope decides where a name is visible. JavaScript uses lexical scope: what you can see is fixed by where the code is written, not where it is called.

Kinds of scope

ScopeCreated byHolds
GlobalThe program / scriptGlobals, globalThis properties
ModuleEach ES module fileTop-level declarations of that module (not global!)
FunctionEvery function callParameters, var, inner declarations
Block{ }, if, for, try…let, const, class (and function declarations in strict mode)

The scope chain

When a name is used, the engine looks in the current scope, then the enclosing one, and so on out to global. The first match wins (shadowing); if none matches → ReferenceError.

Lexical, not dynamic

Accidental globals

What is hoisting?

During the creation phase of a scope, declarations are registered before code executes. Function declarations are available in full, vars start as undefined, and let/const/class exist but stay uninitialised (TDZ) until their line runs. Nothing is physically moved.

What is lexical scoping?

A function's accessible variables are determined by where it is written in the source. Each function remembers the scope it was created in — which is exactly what makes closures possible.
